abstract: We present a compact, height-balanced trie data structure implemented in Aether-Flux that supports insertion of words with associated frequencies and provides frequency-ranked auto-completion queries. The design preserves a key-ordered invariant and a height-balance property that guarantees logarithmic search and insertion times with respect to the number of distinct prefixes. We formally prove that the stored frequency at each node equals the maximum frequency of any word sharing that prefix, and we show that the depth of the trie is bounded by the length of the longest inserted word. Static analysis of the Aether-Flux source yields an AST complexity profile of 158 SLOC and 12 function blocks, confirming the theoretical $O(\log N)$ bounds.
